name: password-generator
title: Password generator
description: Make a strong password or passphrase on demand: length, character sets, copy and regenerate, using the browser's secure random source.

/** The default word list: unique, lower case, in the order written. */
export const DEFAULT_WORDLIST: readonly string[] = [...new Set(WORDS.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean))];

docs: onUse is called with the password when Use this password is pressed; the button is only there when you give it. defaultMode is password or passphrase and defaultLength the length it starts at: characters for a password (12 to 64, default 20) and words for a passphrase (3 to 8, default 6). A password is made from the length, the numbers and symbols switches and Avoid look-alikes (I l 1 | O 0 o), and every set that is on is used at least once; a passphrase is words drawn from wordlist (default: over a thousand everyday words, about ten bits each, and the estimate follows the list you give) with a capital on each and, if you like, one digit. Every character and every word comes from crypto.getRandomValues through rejection sampling, so none is likelier than another, and nothing is sent, stored or logged; where the browser has no secure random source the field says so instead of making a weak password. Nothing is made while rendering, so the server never produces a password: it appears as soon as the page is on screen. The strength is stated as bits, a word (Weak, Fair, Strong, Very strong) and a sentence from the entropy and a billion guesses a second (Would take centuries at a billion guesses a second). Digits are drawn in weight and symbols in a lighter tone so look-alikes are easy to tell apart. Each new result is announced once, politely, without reading the password aloud. The box keeps its height from one result to the next, so Regenerate and Copy stay under the pointer: a password is broken at any character, so a length always takes the same lines, and a passphrase keeps room for words of a typical length. label names the result for a screen reader (default Generated password), and locale writes the numbers (a tag that is not a language tag, such as en_US, is read as en-US). It needs nothing from a Password input, so it also serves an admin screen that sets a temporary password. secureRandom, generatePassword, generatePassphrase, passwordEntropy and guessTime are plain functions in password-generator/generate.
